newsitem.title: USA: InterDigital Pakistan Telecom deal lapses.
newsitem.headline: InterDigital Pakistan Telecom deal lapses.

text.p: InterDigital Communications Corp said its contract with the Pakistan Telecommunications Co Ltd (PTCL) has lapsed, effective Monday.

The contract, valued at $43 million, was for its UltraPhone digital wireless local loop systems. PTCL allowed the contract to lapse when it did not accept InterDigital's proposal to finance the order, InterDigital said.

The contract was awarded to InterDigital in September 1996 and was subject to the final commitment of financing, which InterDigital said it had expected to be provided by the Export-Import Bank of the United States.
In November 1996, the Export-Import Bank opted not to provide financing to support business transactions in Pakistan because of the high degree of economic instability there.

After extending the contract to June 16, 1997, InterDigital said it presented a range of financing alternatives to PTCL on terms it believed were equal to or better than those originally agreed to in the contract.
"We are obviously very disappointed that the contract has lapsed," said William Doyle, President of InterDigital.

"Together with Siemens, we will continue to try to work through the issues associated with this contract with PTCL but we cannot say with any degree of certainty whether we will be able to reestablish the agreement," Doyle said.
"We are very actively pursuing new business opportunities in a number of countries now and we are quite confident we will capture additional orders for UltraPhone systems this year," Doyle said.
InterDigital has developed the UltraPhone in conjunction with Siemens AG.
